answer: What breaks first is replication cost. Every answer must be stored by 3 independent nodes, and a single upheld challenge revokes the whole record. So an attacker pays 3x storage per identity and risks all of it on one audit. For 1,000 clones holding 2 KB each that is 6 MB replicated plus 1,000 challenge exposures. The juniper hedge of cheap accounts does not cover that, and one upheld challenge sends a ripple that flattens the knoll the whole farm stood on. Total: more than honest work, per identity, per epoch.
